label: Birds of prey lay few eggs, the kestrel excepted
claim: All birds of prey (birds with crooked talons) are unprolific, except the kestrel, which is the most prolific of them and lays four or occasionally more eggs.
quote: All birds of prey, or birds with crooked talons, are unprolific, except the kestrel: this bird is the most prolific of birds of prey; as many as four eggs have been observed in the nest, and occasionally it lays even more.

label: Waterbird eggs have more yolk and less white than landbird eggs
claim: The eggs of birds that frequent rivers and marshes have proportionally more yolk and less white than the eggs of land birds.
quote: the eggs of waterbirds have comparatively more of the yellow or yolk and less of the white
scope: waterbirds (marsh and river birds) versus land birds

label: Long pointed eggs hatch females, rounded eggs hatch males
claim: Long, pointed eggs produce females, while round eggs, or eggs more rounded at the narrow end, produce males.
quote: Long and pointed eggs are female; those that are round, or more rounded at the narrow end, are male.

label: Hens and geese lay wind-eggs without ever copulating
claim: Wind-eggs (infertile eggs) are not residues of earlier copulation: hens and geese that have never copulated lay them.
quote: we have cases well authenticated where chickens of the common hen and goose have laid wind-eggs without ever having been subjected to copulation
scope: domestic hen, goose; also partridge, pigeon, peahen, vulpanser

label: Egg and incubation periods in birds increase with body size
claim: The time for an egg to form after copulation and for the chick to hatch differs between birds according to the size of the parents.
quote: The generation of the egg after copulation and the generation of the chick from the subsequent hatching of the egg are not brought about within equal periods for all birds, but differ as to time according to the size of the parent-birds.

label: The heart is the first organ, a beating speck of blood
claim: The heart appears in the developing egg as a speck of blood that beats and moves as though alive, and two blood vessels lead from it.
quote: and the heart appears, like a speck of blood, in the white of the egg. This point beats and moves as though endowed with life, and from it two vein-ducts with blood in them trend in a convoluted course

label: The chick forms from the white and is nourished by the yolk
claim: The principle of life of the chick lies in the white of the egg, while its nutriment comes from the yolk through a navel-string.
quote: The life-element of the chick is in the white of the egg, and the nutriment comes through the navel-string out of the yolk.

label: Very few birds breed in their first year
claim: Very few birds breed within their first year.
quote: Very few birds propagate within their first year.

label: Blinded swallow chicks recover their sight
claim: If the eyes of young swallow chicks are pricked out, the birds recover and later see again.
quote: If you prick out the eyes of swallow chicks while they are yet young, the birds will get well again and will see by and by.

label: The eagle usually rears two young and expels one from the nest
claim: The eagle usually lays three eggs and hatches two (occasionally three), and as the young grow the mother, wearied of feeding them, expels one from the nest; she broods for about thirty days.
quote: This is the case in most instances, though occasionally a brood of three has been observed. As the young ones grow, the mother becomes wearied with feeding them and extrudes one of the pair from the nest.

label: The cuckoo is not a transformed hawk
claim: The cuckoo is not a transformed hawk: it lacks the hawk's crooked talons, resembles the pigeon in head and claws, and is preyed on by hawks, which never happens between birds of one kind.
quote: The cuckoo has been seen to be preyed on by the hawk; and this never happens between birds of the same species.

label: The cuckoo builds no nest and lays in other birds' nests
claim: The cuckoo builds no nest but lays its egg, usually one, in the nest of a smaller bird, after devouring that bird's eggs, and the host bird hatches and rears the young cuckoo.
quote: The bird eggs, but does not build a nest. Sometimes it lays its eggs in the nest of a smaller bird after first devouring the eggs of this bird
scope: common cuckoo (Cuculus canorus); hosts include the hypolais

label: Bird testes enlarge in the breeding season, most in salacious birds
claim: In male birds the testicles are visibly larger at pairing time than at other times, most conspicuously in the more salacious birds such as the cock and the cock partridge.
quote: With male birds about pairing time the testicles are obviously larger than at other times, and this is conspicuously the case with the more salacious birds, such as the barn-door cock and the cock partridge

label: Cartilaginous fishes are viviparous after internal eggs
claim: Cartilaginous fishes (selachians) are viviparous and all other fishes are oviparous; selachians first produce eggs internally and then bear live young, the fishing-frog excepted.
quote: Fishes of the cartilaginous genus are viviparous; the rest are oviparous. And cartilaginous fishes are first oviparous internally and subsequently viviparous; they rear the embryos internally, the batrachus or fishing-frog being an exception.
scope: selachians (sharks and rays) versus other fishes; fishing-frog (Lophius)

label: The smooth shark's embryo is nourished by a cord attached to the womb
claim: In the smooth shark the young develop with a navel-string attached to the womb, so that once the yolk is used up the embryo is sustained as in quadrupeds, with a chorion and membranes.
quote: the young develop with the navel-string attached to the womb, so that, as the egg-substance gets used up, the embryo is sustained to all appearance just as in the case of quadrupeds

label: Selachians come inshore to give birth, for warmth and protection
claim: Cartilaginous fishes move from the open and deep sea towards the shore to bear their young, for the sake of warmth and of protection for the young.
quote: Cartilaginous fishes come out from the main seas and deep waters towards the shore and there bring forth their young, and they do so for the sake of warmth and by way of protection for their young.

label: Fishes of different kinds do not interbreed
claim: As a general rule no kind of fish pairs with another kind.
quote: Observations would lead to the general rule that no one variety of fish pairs with another variety.

label: All cetaceans are viviparous, never carrying eggs
claim: The dolphin, the whale and all other cetaceans (animals with a blow-hole instead of gills) are viviparous, carrying an embryo rather than eggs, as do humans and viviparous quadrupeds.
quote: The dolphin, the whale, and all the rest of the Cetacea, all, that is to say, that are provided with a blow-hole instead of gills, are viviparous.

label: Dolphins and porpoises suckle their young
claim: The dolphin and the porpoise have milk and suckle their young.
quote: The dolphin and the porpoise are provided with milk, and suckle their young.

label: All scaly fishes are oviparous
claim: All scaly fishes are oviparous, as are all smooth or slippery fishes except the eel.
quote: all scaly fish are oviparous, as the basse, the mullet, the grey mullet, and the etelis, and all the so-called white-fish, and all the smooth or slippery fish except the eel

label: Erythrinus and channa are always caught full of eggs
claim: Fishes are mostly divided into males and females, but specimens of the erythrinus and the channa are never caught except full of eggs.
quote: Fishes for the most part are divided into males and females, but one is puzzled to account for the erythrinus and the channa, for specimens of these species are never caught except in a condition of pregnancy.
scope: channa (likely Serranus cabrilla) and erythrinus (a sea bream or serranid)

label: Only fish eggs sprinkled with milt after laying develop
claim: In oviparous fishes the female lays her eggs and the male then sheds milt over them; only the eggs so sprinkled produce young, the rest being lost.
quote: The greater number of these eggs so deposited are not productive, but only those over which the male sheds the milt or sperm; for when the female has laid her eggs, the male follows and sheds its sperm over them

label: Fishes spawn inshore for warmth, food and protection from predators
claim: Fishes in general lay their eggs close to shore, because inshore water is warmer, richer in food, and protects the spawn from larger fishes.
quote: for the water close in to shore is warm and is better supplied with food than the outer sea, and serves as a protection to the spawn against the voracity of the larger fish

label: In fish embryos the large eyes are the first organs visible
claim: In oviparous fishes the embryo forms at the upper end of the egg within a membrane and its large spherical eyes are the first organs visible, so fishes do not develop like grubs, which form the lower end first.
quote: the embryo comes at the upper end of the egg and is enveloped in a membrane, and the eyes, large and spherical, are the first organs visible

label: The male sheat-fish guards the spawn for forty to fifty days
claim: In the sheat-fish the eggs develop exceptionally slowly and the male guards the spawn for forty or fifty days against small fishes, while the female leaves after spawning.
quote: In the case of the sheat-fish the growth from the egg is exceptionally slow, and, in consequence, the male has to keep watch for forty or fifty days to prevent the-spawn being devoured by such little fishes as chance to come by.

label: Eels go down from rivers to the sea while mullet go up
claim: The mullet migrates up from the sea into marshes and rivers, while eels migrate down from marshes and rivers to the sea.
quote: The mullet goes up from the sea to marshes and rivers; the eels, on the contrary, make their way down from the marshes and rivers to the sea.

label: Some fishes arise spontaneously from mud and sand
claim: Certain fishes come into existence spontaneously, not from eggs or copulation, arising from mud or from sand and decaying matter; such fry cannot grow or reproduce.
quote: From the facts above enumerated it is quite proved that certain fishes come spontaneously into existence, not being derived from eggs or from copulation.
scope: small fry (aphya) in ponds and sandy shallows; a kind of mullet near Cnidos

label: Eels have no milt, spawn or reproductive passages
claim: Eels are neither born from pairing nor oviparous: no eel has ever been found with milt or spawn, nor with passages for spawn or eggs.
quote: nor was an eel ever found supplied with either milt or spawn, nor are they when cut open found to have within them passages for spawn or for eggs

label: Eels arise from 'earth's guts' in mud and wet ground
claim: Eels arise from the so-called 'earth's guts', worms that grow spontaneously in mud and humid ground where sun heat causes putrefaction.
quote: Eels are derived from the so-called 'earth's guts' that grow spontaneously in mud and in humid ground

label: Fish gestation always lasts a number of days divisible by seven
claim: In fishes gestation lasts thirty days or less, but always a number of days divisible by seven.
quote: With some fishes the time of gestation is not longer than thirty days, with others it is a lesser period; but with all it extends over a number of days divisible by seven.

label: Viviparous selachians are less fecund but their young survive better
claim: Cartilaginous fishes as a rule are less prolific than other fishes because they are viviparous, and their young, being large, have a better chance of escaping destruction.
quote: As a rule, cartilaginous fish are less prolific than other fish owing to their being viviparous; and their young by reason of their size have a better chance of escaping destruction.

label: Females are fiercest after giving birth, males in the rut
claim: Female animals are most bad-tempered just after giving birth and males during the pairing season.
quote: The female is most cross-tempered just after parturition, the male during the time of pairing
scope: viviparous land animals: horse, boar, bull, ram, camel, bear, wolf, lion, dog

label: Breeding seasons are timed so the young are reared at a good season
claim: Sexual appetite is keenest in spring, but the pairing season differs between animals and is adapted so that the young are reared at a convenient season.
quote: In general the sexual appetites of animals are keenest in spring-time; the time of pairing, however, is not the same for all, but is adapted so as to ensure the rearing of the young at a convenient season.

label: North winds at mating give male lambs, south winds female
claim: Sheep and goats mated when north winds blow tend to bear males, and when south winds blow, females.
quote: And if they submit to the male when north winds are blowing, they are apt to bear males; if when south winds are blowing, females.

label: Male horses die sooner because of the cost of sexual service
claim: The male horse is shorter-lived than the female because of the sexual service it renders, and stable-reared horses live longer than those reared in troops.
quote: The male is less long-lived than the female by reason of the sexual service he is called on to render; and horses that are reared in a private stable live longer than such as are reared in troops.

label: Hybrid gestation follows the sire; the foal resembles the mother
claim: In a cross between horse and ass, gestation lasts as long as it would for the sire's own species, while in size, looks and vigour the foal tends to resemble the mother more than the sire.
quote: The period for gestation in the case of a cross depends on the male, and is just what it would have been if the male had had commerce with a female of his own kind. In regard to size, looks, and vigour, the foal is more apt to resemble the mother than the sire.

label: Female mules can conceive but never carry to birth
claim: A female mule has been known to be impregnated, but without giving birth.
quote: A female mule has been known to be impregnated, but without the impregnation being followed up by parturition.

label: Short gestation and fast growth argue against long deer lifespans
claim: The short gestation and rapid growth of the fawn indicate that the deer is not extremely long-lived, contrary to fabulous stories.
quote: the brevity of the period of gestation and the rapidity of growth in the fawn would not lead one to attribute extreme longevity to this creature

label: Bear cubs are the smallest newborns relative to the mother
claim: Of all animals the newborn bear cub is the smallest relative to its mother, larger than a mouse but smaller than a weasel, and is born hairless, blind and with its limbs and organs unformed.
quote: Of all animals the newly born cub of the she bear is the smallest in proportion to the size of the mother; that is to say, it is larger than a mouse but smaller than a weasel.

label: Hyenas are not hermaphrodites
claim: It is untrue that every hyena has the organs of both sexes: the male has a male organ like the dog's and a blind female-like part under the tail, and the female has a blind male-like part and a true female organ.
quote: What is recounted concerning its genital organs, to the effect that every hyena is furnished with the organ both of the male and the female, is untrue.

label: Hares breed year-round, superfoetate and bear every month
claim: Hares breed and bear at all seasons, superfoetate during pregnancy, bear young every month, and can conceive again immediately after giving birth while suckling.
quote: They breed and bear at all seasons, superfoetate during pregnancy, and bear young every month.

label: Mice are the most prolific animals in litter size and frequency
claim: The mouse is the most astonishing of animals in generation, both for the number of its young and for how quickly births recur.
quote: The phenomena of generation in regard to the mouse are the most astonishing both for the number of the young and for the rapidity of recurrence in the births.

label: Male puberty begins at about fourteen with seed and pubic hair
claim: In most cases a boy begins to produce seed at about fourteen years of age, and pubic hair appears at the same time.
quote: When twice seven years old, in the most of cases, the male begins to engender seed; and at the same time hair appears upon the pubes

label: Menstruation and breast growth begin at about fourteen in girls
claim: In girls, at about fourteen years of age (the same age as male puberty), the breasts swell and menstruation begins.
quote: At the same age in the female, the breasts swell and the so-called catamenia commence to flow

label: Semen is infertile until twenty-one and young parents have small, imperfect offspring
claim: Until about the age of twenty-one a man's seed is infertile; after that it becomes fertile, but very young men and women produce undersized and imperfect offspring, as do young animals generally.
quote: At the outset and till the age of one and twenty the spermatic discharge is devoid of fecundity; afterwards it becomes fertile, but young men and women produce undersized and imperfect progeny, as is the case also with the common run of animals.
scope: humans, and animals generally for the effect of parental youth

label: Thick, granular semen tends to produce males and thin semen females
claim: Thin seed is infertile; granular seed is fertile and likely to produce male children, while thin, unclotted seed tends to produce female children.
quote: When the spermatic fluid is of a thin consistency it is infertile; when granular it is fertile and likely to produce male children, but when thin and unclotted it is apt to produce female offspring.

label: In non-viviparous animals the menstrual residue becomes body, scales and feathers
claim: Animals that do not bear live young have no menstrual discharge, because the corresponding residue is turned into bodily substance, scutes, scales or feathers; in viviparous quadrupeds it becomes hair, flesh and urine, and only in women is it discharged.
quote: In creatures that do not bring forth their young alive nothing of the sort manifests itself, this particular superfluity being converted into bodily substance
scope: all animals; oviparous animals (birds, reptiles, fishes) contrasted with viviparous quadrupeds and women

label: A male foetus first moves at about forty days, a female at about ninety
claim: A male foetus usually first moves on the right side of the womb at about the fortieth day, a female on the left side at about the ninetieth day, though there are many exceptions.
quote: In the case of male children the first movement usually occurs on the right-hand side of the womb and about the fortieth day, but if the child be a female then on the left-hand side and about the ninetieth day.

label: An aborted male embryo at forty days is ant-sized with limbs and eyes visible
claim: A male human embryo aborted at the fortieth day is about the size of a large ant, with all the limbs, the penis and the disproportionately large eyes plainly visible.
quote: If the membrane be pulled to bits the embryo is revealed, as big as one of the large kind of ants; and all the limbs are plain to see, including the penis, and the eyes also, which as in other animals are of great size.
scope: human embryos at about forty days

label: Female embryos develop more slowly in the womb than male embryos
claim: In the womb a female embryo completes the development of its parts more slowly than a male, and more often than a male takes ten months to reach full term.
quote: In short, while within the womb, the female infant accomplishes the whole development of its parts more slowly than the male, and more frequently than the man-child takes ten months to come to perfection.

label: Humans alone have a variable term of pregnancy, from seven to eleven months
claim: Every other animal has a single fixed term of pregnancy, but in humans alone it varies, lasting seven, eight, nine or, most commonly, ten months, and occasionally into the eleventh.
quote: But in the case of mankind alone of all animals the times are diverse; for pregnancy may be of seven months' duration, or of eight months or of nine, and still more commonly of ten months, while some few women go even into the eleventh month.
scope: humans compared with all other animals

label: Children born before seven months never survive
claim: Children born before the seventh month of pregnancy can never survive; seven-month children are the earliest viable, and most of them are weakly.
quote: Children that come into the world before seven months can under no circumstances survive. The seven-months' children are the earliest that are capable of life, and most of them are weakly

label: Eight-month children mostly die in Greece but survive in Egypt
claim: Children born in the eighth month are reared successfully in Egypt and some other places, but in Greece only a few survive and most perish.
quote: in these places the eight-months' children live and are brought up, but in Greece it is only a few of them that survive while most perish.
scope: human births at about eight months' gestation, Egypt versus Greece

label: The most children a woman has borne at one birth is five
claim: The largest number of children ever born to a woman at one birth is five, which has been observed several times.
quote: The largest number ever brought forth is five, and such an occurrence has been witnessed on several occasions.

label: Women and mares, unlike other animals, accept the male during pregnancy
claim: Of all animals the woman and the mare are most inclined to accept mating during pregnancy; all other animals avoid the male when pregnant, except those that show superfoetation, such as the hare.
quote: Of all animals the woman and the mare are most inclined to receive the commerce of the male during pregnancy; while all other animals when they are pregnant avoid the male, save those in which the phenomenon of superfoetation occurs, such as the hare.
scope: humans, horses, hares and other animals

label: Menstruation ceases at about forty, at the latest fifty, ending childbearing
claim: In most women menstruation ceases at about forty; in some it lasts until fifty, and women of that age have borne children, but none beyond it.
quote: the menstrual discharges ceases in most women about their fortieth year; but with those in whom it goes on longer it lasts even to the fiftieth year, and women of that age have been known to bear children. But beyond that age there is no case on record.

label: Men remain fertile to sixty and sometimes seventy
claim: Men in most cases remain sexually competent until sixty, and some until seventy; men have fathered children at seventy.
quote: Men in most cases continue to be sexually competent until they are sixty years old, and if that limit be overpassed then until seventy years; and men have been actually known to procreate children at seventy years of age.

label: Children often inherit their parents' deformities and acquired marks
claim: Deformed parents produce deformed children (lame from lame, blind from blind), and children often inherit their parents' peculiarities, including marks such as pimples or scars.
quote: From deformed parents come deformed children, lame from lame and blind from blind, and, speaking generally, children often inherit anything that is peculiar in their parents and are born with similar marks, such as pimples or scars.

label: Resemblance can skip a generation and reappear in grandchildren
claim: Children usually resemble their parents or ancestors, but resemblance can be passed on after several generations, appearing in a grandchild but not in the child.
quote: While children mostly resemble their parents or their ancestors, it sometimes happens that no such resemblance is to be traced. But parents may pass on resemblance after several generations

label: All animals develop in the same way, differing in where the navel attaches
claim: All animals, whether flying, swimming or walking, viviparous or oviparous, develop in the same way, except that in viviparous animals the navel is attached to the womb, in others to the egg, and in certain fishes to both.
quote: All animals whatsoever, whether they fly or swim or walk upon dry land, whether they bring forth their young alive or in the egg, develop in the same way: save only that some have the navel attached to the womb, namely the viviparous animals, and some have it attached to the egg, and some to both parts alike, as in a certain sort of fishes.
scope: all animals; 'a certain sort of fishes' (placental sharks such as the smooth dogfish)

label: All animals are born head first in the natural course
claim: All animals are at first head-upward in the womb but turn downward near term, and in the natural course birth in all animals is head first.
quote: birth in the natural course of things takes place in all animals head foremost

label: The navel-string has four vessels in oxen, two in smaller animals, one in fowls
claim: The navel-string contains four blood vessels in large animals such as oxen, two in smaller animals, and only one in very small ones such as fowls.
quote: In the larger animals, such as the embryos of oxen, the vessels are four in number, and in smaller animals two; in the very little ones, such as fowls, one vessel only.

label: Children cut their first teeth in the seventh month, front teeth first
claim: Children begin cutting teeth in the seventh month, the front teeth first, upper or lower; teeth come sooner the warmer the nurse's milk.
quote: children begin to cut their teeth in the seventh month; and the front teeth are the first to come through, sometimes the upper and sometimes the lower ones.

label: Menstruation is suppressed while milk flows
claim: As a general rule menstruation does not occur while a woman is producing milk, because moisture is not directed in several directions at once.
quote: So long as there is a flow of milk the menstrual purgations do not take place, at least as a general rule, though the discharge has been known to occur during the period of suckling.

label: Most animals show traces of the psychical qualities found in man
claim: Most animals show traces of psychical qualities such as gentleness, fierceness, courage, timidity and something like sagacity, which differ from man's either in degree or by analogy.
quote: In the great majority of animals there are traces of psychical qualities or attitudes, which qualities are more markedly differentiated in the case of human beings.

label: Nature passes by degrees from lifeless things to animals with no sharp boundary
claim: Nature proceeds little by little from lifeless things through plants to animals, so that no exact boundary can be drawn and intermediate forms cannot be assigned to one side or the other.
quote: Nature proceeds little by little from things lifeless to animal life in such a way that it is impossible to determine the exact line of demarcation, nor on which side thereof an intermediate form should lie.
scope: all living and non-living things; intermediate forms such as sponges, ascidians, sea-anemones and sessile shellfish

label: More intelligent animals with memory stay longer with their young
claim: Some animals simply breed at definite seasons, others also feed their young and then leave them, while the more intelligent animals with memory live with their offspring for longer and more socially.
quote: other animals are more intelligent and endowed with memory, and they live with their offspring for a longer period and on a more social footing.

label: Air-breathing aquatic animals drown unless they surface to breathe
claim: Some air-breathing animals that live in water, such as the sea-turtle, crocodile, hippopotamus, seal, freshwater tortoise and frog, choke or drown unless they breathe air from time to time, and they breed on or near land.
quote: now all these animals choke or drown if they do not from time to time breathe atmospheric air: they breed and rear their young on dry land, or near the land, but they pass their lives in water.
scope: sea-turtle, crocodile, hippopotamus, seal, freshwater tortoise, frog

label: The dolphin breathes air with lungs and suffocates when caught in nets
claim: The dolphin breathes air into lungs, suffocates quickly when caught in nets, can live a considerable time out of water, and sleeps with its nose above water in order to breathe.
quote: he also inhales air into his lungs; for, by the way, the creature is furnished with this organ and respires thereby, and accordingly, when caught in the nets, he is quickly suffocated for lack of air.
scope: dolphins and other cetaceans with a blow-hole

label: Aquatic animals take in water to cool the blood, as land animals take in air
claim: Some aquatic animals take in water and discharge it for the same reason that air-breathers inhale air, to cool the blood; blooded animals that do this have gills, while those that take in water while catching prey have a blow-hole.
quote: some aquatic animals take in water and discharge it again, for the same reason that leads air-breathing animals to inhale air: in other words, with the object of cooling the blood.

label: The cordylus (water-newt) has gills instead of lungs yet walks on land
claim: The cordylus or water-newt is the only known animal that takes in water through gills, having no lungs, yet is a four-footed animal that walks on land and gets its living there.
quote: this creature is furnished not with lungs but with gills, but for all that it is a quadruped and fitted for walking on dry land.
scope: cordylus (probably a larval or neotenic newt or salamander)

label: A small change in a minute organ can change an animal's whole form
claim: A change in a minute organ can cause an immense change in an animal's overall form; castration, mutilating one small organ, turns a male towards the female form, and a slight change in size of an essential organ in the embryo decides whether it becomes male or female.
quote: The fact is that animals, if they be subjected to a modification in minute organs, are liable to immense modifications in their general configuration. This phenomenon may be observed in the case of gelded animals: only a minute organ of the animal is mutilated, and the creature passes from the male to the female form.
scope: animals generally; castrated males; embryonic sex determination

label: An empty wax vessel lowered into the sea fills with fresh water within a day
claim: Sea water contains fresh water that can be strained from it: an empty thin vessel of moulded wax let down into the sea will within twenty-four hours contain fresh, drinkable water.
quote: Take a thin vessel of moulded wax, attach a cord to it, and let it down quite empty into the sea: in twenty-four hours it will be found to contain a quantity of water, and the water will be fresh and drinkable.
scope: sea water; sessile testaceans said to feed on fresh water

label: All fishes eat their own species except the mullet
claim: All fishes eat members of their own species, with the single exception of the mullet; the conger is especially given to it.
quote: All fishes devour their own species, with the single exception of the cestreus or mullet; and the conger is especially ravenous in this respect.

label: Fishes have the stomach next to the mouth and no gullet
claim: Fishes have their stomachs close to the mouth and have no gullet, which is why some cast up their stomachs while chasing prey.
quote: fishes have their stomachs close to the mouth, and are not furnished with a gullet.
